questions.prompt: When does a bulb light up?
options: Cell and bulb form a loop
questions.why: The bulb lights up only when it is connected to the cell with a complete path.
questions.quote: In Practical 8.1, the bulb only lights up when it is connected to the cell with connecting wires to form a complete path.

questions.prompt: Which of these is an electrical insulator?
questions.why: Plastics, wood and distilled water do not conduct electricity.
questions.quote: Plastics, wood and distilled water do not conduct electricity. They are electrical insulators.

questions.prompt: Which circuit type has a complete path?
questions.why: A circuit with a complete path is a closed circuit.
questions.quote: A circuit with a complete path is called a closed circuit.

questions.prompt: What does a switch do in a circuit?
questions.why: A switch opens or closes an electrical circuit.
questions.quote: A switch is used to open or close an electrical circuit.

questions.prompt: What is a material that conducts electricity called?
questions.why: Materials that conduct electricity are electrical conductors.
questions.quote: Materials that conduct electricity are electrical conductors.

questions.prompt: Which of these materials conducts electricity?
questions.why: Metals, pencil lead (graphite) and vinegar conduct electricity.
questions.quote: For example, metals, pencil lead (graphite) and vinegar conduct electricity.

questions.prompt: What does the bulb produce from electrical energy?
questions.why: The bulb converts electrical energy into light energy and thermal energy.
questions.quote: The bulb converts electrical energy to light energy and thermal energy.

questions.prompt: What is a diagram showing component connections called?
questions.why: A circuit diagram shows how components are connected.
questions.quote: A circuit diagram shows how circuit components are connected.

questions.prompt: What energy does a cell store?
questions.why: A cell stores chemical energy, which is converted into electrical energy.
questions.quote: Chemical energy stored in the cell is converted to electrical energy.

questions.prompt: What does the circuit transfer from the cell to the bulb?
questions.why: The circuit transfers electrical energy from the cell to the bulb.
questions.quote: The circuit transfers electrical energy from the cell to the bulb.

questions.prompt: What does the term battery refer to?
options: A cell or several cells linked
questions.why: A battery can be a single cell or several cells connected together.
questions.quote: A battery refers to a single cell or several cells connected together.

questions.prompt: Which of these can serve as a source of electrical energy?
questions.why: Generators and solar panels are sources of electrical energy.
questions.quote: Other energy sources include a generator and a solar panel.

questions.prompt: What is the first condition for an appliance to work?
questions.why: The first condition is a source of electrical energy.
questions.quote: The first condition for an appliance to work is the presence of a source of electrical energy.

questions.prompt: Are the switches in a keyboard normally open or closed?
questions.why: The switches in keyboard keys are kept open until pressed.
questions.quote: The switches are kept open.

questions.prompt: What parts does a switch contain?
questions.why: A switch has both conducting and insulating parts.
questions.quote: There are conducting and insulating parts in the switch (Fig 8.7).

questions.prompt: What do standard circuit symbols represent?
questions.why: Standard circuit symbols represent different circuit components.
questions.quote: We use some standard circuit symbols to represent different circuit components of a circuit.

questions.prompt: What should be placed at each wire junction when drawing a circuit diagram?
questions.why: A solid dot marks each wire junction in a circuit diagram.
questions.quote: Put a solid dot at each wire junction.

questions.prompt: Is a switch a necessary component to form a complete circuit?
questions.why: A switch is not required; a complete circuit needs only a source and a closed loop.
questions.quote: A switch is a necessary component to form a complete circuit.

questions.prompt: What happens to a torch when its switch is opened?
questions.why: Opening the switch breaks the circuit, so the torch goes off.
questions.quote: (b) when the switch is open, the circuit is incomplete and the torch goes off

questions.prompt: What happens if an LED is connected directly to the cell?
questions.why: Connecting the LED directly to the cell can damage it.
questions.quote: Never connect the LED to the cell directly. Otherwise, the LED will be damaged.
